declared_function.evidence: spaces/app.py declares one @spaces.GPU(duration=120) function; the job's record line names hosting='ZeroGPU hardware; one @spaces.GPU function is declared for the startup check and no job calls it, so a job spends 0 GPU seconds'; tests/test_space_stage.py::test_the_app_declares_one_gpu_function_and_no_job_calls_it pins both facts

gpu.platform_constraint: ZeroGPU refuses to start a Space with no @spaces.GPU function at all: the first boot of this tree died RUNTIME_ERROR with 'No @spaces.GPU function detected during startup'

measured_dead_end.design: the CPU edit wrapped in @spaces.GPU(duration=120), the shape §4's decision rule prescribes for an edit that fits one call
measured_dead_end.result: the job finished its download in 3 s and then never started the edit: it sat queued for a GPU card the edit cannot use, with no output for >10 minutes, and the 120 s cap never fired because the call had not been admitted. Recorded as a dead end, not as a runtime.
measured_dead_end.conclusion: on the free tier a CPU-only edit must not be routed through the GPU queue: it converts a 16-minute CPU job into a 16-minute CPU job behind an unbounded GPU wait

output.floor_note: the type ladder admitted Q6_K from its sampled preview and the whole-tensor read-back came in at 0.8808, below the entry's 0.95 floor; the delivered card states 0.8808 and claims codec fidelity only. This is the same sample-vs-whole-tensor gap the self-apply card recorded on the base's Q8_0 (sample 0.9974, whole tensor 0.8812). The file was still delivered because the loop's contract is to hand over the artifact it measured with its number on the card, under the banked_unmeasured label — but a Q8_0 edit clears where Q6_K does not, so the ladder's preview threshold is the defect to fix
